Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: bounded OIDC retry in the Claude pool token step (unblocks #8481)

Planning ref: `a28124d4c807d5891faff4bc10d77210f51bcb0f` on `main`. "Integration branch mismatch" reads `unknown`, not `true`, so this is not blocked.

Clarification mapping: no questions were asked and the answer was auto-posted. The scope comes from the unblock judge's fix-up text, which is based on the #8481 clarify answers: Q1 A (bounded retry), Q2 A (the retry goes inside `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`) and Q3 A (only the OIDC request is retried).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/claude_pool_token.sh
Scope-mode justification: The fix-up spells out the full change: one retry loop around the existing OIDC request, one new entry in the fixed tuple `ENGINE_FALLBACK_SCOPE_PATHS`, and four named test cases on the existing `_Stub` OIDC server. The plan delivers exactly that, plus a changelog fragment for the change in behaviour. The broker POST, the pool probes and `orchestrate_poll_process.sh` are left alone. Two cheap additions make it complete rather than a shortcut, each under 30 lines with no new dependency or interface: a test that an invalid flag value turns the retry off with a warning (the spec requires that warning), and a test pinning the new scope-tuple entry. Following §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the completeness that improves correctness wins over the shorter diff. No existing helper retries an HTTP call with this exact status policy and secret-free logging; the loop is a local extension of the script's own curl call. Using `gh_retry` from `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` would wrap `gh`, not curl with a header file, and could put tokens in argv.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`
- `tests/test_claude_pool_token.py`
- `changelog.d/8484-claude-pool-oidc-retry.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

**1. `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`, step "2. The OIDC token" (currently lines 120-126)**

- **Header comment:** add two entries to the "Inputs (environment)" list:
  - `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_ENABLED`: default on.
  - `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_SLEEPS`: default `'2 5'`.
- **Flag parsing** goes near the other input defaults (after `probe_timeout`, before the pool-dir checks). Use new locals with unique names (checked against the file): `oidc_retry_raw`, `oidc_retry_on`, `oidc_retry_sleeps`, `oidc_attempt`, `oidc_max_attempts`.
  - `oidc_retry_raw="${CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_ENABLED:-}"`, then lowercase it with `${oidc_retry_raw,,}`.
  - Empty or `true` sets `oidc_retry_on=true`. `false` sets it to `false`.
  - Any other value sets it to `false` and prints `::warning::claude_pool_token.sh: CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_ENABLED is neither true nor false; OIDC retry off` to stderr. The raw value is never echoed, so a value cannot inject a workflow command or leak.
- **Sleeps:**
  - Read `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_SLEEPS:-2 5` into an array with `read -r -a`.
  - Accept it only if it has exactly 2 entries and each matches `^[0-9]+$` and is ≤ 60.
  - Otherwise fall back to `(2 5)` and log `CLAUDE_POOL oidc_retry_sleeps_invalid fallback=2,5`, without the raw value.
- **Loop**, replacing the single curl call:
  - Write the `oidc-request-headers` file once, exactly as today.
  - `oidc_max_attempts=3` when the retry is on, otherwise `1`. `oidc_attempt=1`.
  - Each iteration runs the same command as today, `curl -sS -o "${work}/oidc.json" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 -H @headers "<url>?audience=…" 2>/dev/null`, with `|| oidc_code="000"`. The curl `-o` truncates the body file on each attempt.
  - Stop if `oidc_code` is `200`, or if `oidc_attempt -ge oidc_max_attempts`.
  - Stop unless the code is one of `000`, `429` or `5[0-9][0-9]` (so 401, 403 and every other code fail at once).
  - Otherwise print `CLAUDE_POOL oidc_retry attempt=$((oidc_attempt+1)) code=${oidc_code}` to stdout, `sleep "${oidc_retry_sleeps[oidc_attempt-1]}"`, increment `oidc_attempt` and continue.
  - After the loop: `rm -f -- "${work}/oidc-request-headers"`, then the unchanged `[ "${oidc_code}" = "200" ] || finish false "oidc_request_failed_${oidc_code}"`.
- **Assumption comment in code:** `attempt=<n>` is the number of the attempt about to be made (2 or 3).
- **Unchanged:** the broker POST, the broker headers, the probes and every `finish` reason.

**2. `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`**

Append `"scripts/claude_pool_token.sh"` to `ENGINE_FALLBACK_SCOPE_PATHS` (lines 110-119), after `".github/actions/claude-pool-token/action.yml"`. Extend the comment above the tuple with one line saying the pool token step is included because its OIDC request decides `no_credential` fallbacks (#8481).

**3. `tests/test_claude_pool_token.py`**

- **`_Stub` changes:**
  - Add a class attribute `oidc_statuses: list[int] = []`.
  - In `do_GET`, when the path and auth match and `_Stub.oidc_statuses` is non-empty, `pop(0)` a status. A popped `200` sends `{"value": JWT}`; any other popped status sends `{}`. When the list is empty, behave as today.
  - The `env` fixture resets `_Stub.oidc_statuses = []`.
- **New tests.** All of them pass `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_SLEEPS="0 0"`. The fixture strips every `CLAUDE_*` variable, so tests set the flag explicitly when needed. GETs are counted with `[s for s in _Stub.seen if s["method"] == "GET"]`.
  - `test_oidc_retry_recovers_after_503`: statuses `[503, 200]`.
    - Ends with `available=true`.
    - 2 GETs are made.
    - stdout contains `CLAUDE_POOL oidc_retry attempt=2 code=503`.
    - stdout and stderr contain neither `REQUEST_TOKEN`, `JWT` nor `audience=`.
  - `test_oidc_retry_gives_up_after_three_503`: statuses `[503, 503, 503, 200]`.
    - Ends with `oidc_request_failed_503`.
    - Exactly 3 GETs and no POST.
  - `test_oidc_401_is_not_retried`: run with `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN="wrong"`.
    - Ends with `oidc_request_failed_401`.
    - 1 GET, and no `oidc_retry` line.
  - `test_oidc_retry_flag_false_makes_one_attempt`: `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_ENABLED="false"`, statuses `[503, 200]`.
    - Ends with `oidc_request_failed_503`.
    - 1 GET.
  - Additional `test_oidc_retry_flag_invalid_is_off_with_warning`: value `maybe`.
    - 1 GET and a `::warning::` on stderr.
    - The value `maybe` does not appear in the output.
  - Additional `test_pool_token_script_is_in_engine_fallback_heal_scope`: import `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` the same way `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` does, and assert the path is in the tuple.
- `test_oidc_request_rejected` is unchanged and still passes.

**4. `changelog.d/8484-claude-pool-oidc-retry.md`**

Use the `<!-- changelog: changed -->` fragment, following the pattern of `changelog.d/8471-ci-action-resolution-rerun.md`. It should say:
- the retry policy, and that 401 and 403 are not retried;
- the off switch and its values;
- that the scope is widened;
- `Refs #8481`, a non-closing reference.

## Data structures affected

- `ENGINE_FALLBACK_SCOPE_PATHS` grows from 8 to 9 paths. `render_heal_scope_marker` caps scopes at 20, so there is no truncation.
- `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` derives its fixtures from the tuple (`_prepare_engine_scope_support`, lines 6915-6918, and the line 6873 existence check). It picks up the new path automatically, and the file exists.
- No changes to schemas, outputs or the reason vocabulary.

## API or interface changes

- New optional env vars, both read only by `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh` and both with in-script defaults (§8): `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_ENABLED` (default on) and `CLAUDE_POOL_OIDC_RETRY_SLEEPS` (default `2 5`).
- `.github/actions/claude-pool-token/main.js` spawns the script with `{ ...process.env }`, so a job-level env value reaches the script without any action change.
- New stdout lines under the registered `CLAUDE_POOL` prefix: `oidc_retry attempt= code=` and `oidc_retry_sleeps_invalid fallback=2,5`.
- GitHub outputs and the `oidc_request_failed_<code>` reasons are unchanged.

Failure modes:

| Trigger | What the job sees | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Transient 5xx, 429 or connection failure (`000`) | `oidc_retry` lines, then `available=true` | Automatic |
| Persistent 5xx | 3 attempts, then `available=false reason=oidc_request_failed_5xx` | Codex fallback, as today |
| 401 or 403 | 1 attempt, same reason as today | Unchanged |

Worst case adds about 67s to the step: 2 extra attempts of up to 30s each, plus 7s of sleep. `main.js` sets no timeout on the spawn.

## Decisions

### D1 — Retry loop placed inline around the existing curl call
- Chosen: a `while` loop in step 2 of `claude_pool_token.sh`. It reuses the same header file and curl flags, and removes the header file once, after the loop.
- Alternatives considered: a generic retry helper in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`; retrying in `main.js`; retrying the whole script.
- Why: Q2 A and Q3 A limit the retry to the OIDC request in this script. A shared helper would widen scope, and retrying the whole script would also repeat the broker POST, which the fix-up forbids.

### D2 — Off switch semantics and safe warning
- Chosen: unset, empty or `true` (any case) is on, `false` is off, and any other value is off with a `::warning::` that does not echo the value.
- Alternatives considered: treating unknown values as on; echoing the value in the warning.
- Why: this matches the fix-up text and the repo's other `_ENABLED` switches, such as `CLAUDE_POOL_CAPACITY_WAIT_ENABLED`. Not echoing the value avoids workflow-command injection and leaking it into logs.

### D3 — `attempt=<n>` counts the upcoming attempt
- Chosen: `attempt=2` or `attempt=3`.
- Alternatives considered: logging the number of the attempt that failed.
- Why: the spec does not define it. Numbering the upcoming attempt reads as "retrying, attempt 2", and the code comment and the test pin it.

### D4 — Validate the sleep list
- Chosen: exactly 2 integers
